summary: James Henry Nelson was an Indologist who earned his M.A. at the University of Cambridge in 1856. He later served as a Fellow at King's College London.

James Hope Moulton studied at the universities of London, Cambridge, and Edinburgh, and under Edward Byles Cowell. Specializing in linguistics, Iranian/Central Asian, and religious studies, he held posts at Didsbury College (1902) and the University of Manchester (1908).

James Irving Manatt was a scholar of linguistics, history, and archaeology. He studied at Grinnell and Yale under William Dwight Whitney. He held positions at Denison, Marietta, University of Nebraska-Lincoln, and served as Professor at Brown University (~1892–1915).

James Ishmael Ford is a scholar in Buddhist and religious studies who earned degrees from Sonoma State and Pacific School of Religion. He trained under Mel Weitsman, Jiyu-Kennett, and John Tarrant, and founded the Boundless Way Zen and Empty Moon Zen networks.

James Kennedy was an Indology, history, and archaeology scholar who studied at the University of Edinburgh. He worked as a missionary for the London Missionary Society (until 1877), lectured at University College London, and served as treasurer of the Royal Asiatic Society.

James Kenneth Powell II is a Buddhist studies scholar who earned degrees from Northwestern, University of Chicago, and University of Wisconsin-Madison (PhD, 1998). His teachers included Geshe Lhundup Sopa, Isshi Yamada, David M. Knipe, and MA supervisor David Tracy.

James L. Fitzgerald, a scholar of Indology and religious studies, earned his PhD at the University of Chicago (1980), studying under J. A. B. van Buitenen and Edwin Gerow. He held professorships at the University of Tennessee, Knoxville and Brown University.

James L. Taylor is a religious and Buddhist studies scholar who earned his PhD from Macquarie University in 1989. He served as Senior Lecturer in Anthropology at the University of Adelaide (attested 2014).

James Legge was a sinologist who studied at Aberdeen Grammar School, the University of Aberdeen, and Highbury College. He served with the London Missionary Society, the Anglo-Chinese College, and as Professor and Fellow at the University of Oxford from 1876 to 1897.

James Liddell Phillips was a linguistics and religious studies scholar. He completed his education at Whitestown Seminary, Bowdoin College (graduate and D.D.), and Columbia University Vagelos College of Physicians and Surgeons (M.D., ~1861–1864).
James Long was a scholar of Indology and linguistics who studied at the Church Missionary Society College, Islington in 1838. In 1840, he was appointed as a missionary for the Church Mission Society.
James Low is a tibetology and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at the University of Edinburgh and received traditional training under Chhimed Rigdzin Rinpoche.

James Luther Adams was a scholar of religious studies and philosophy. He completed his education at the University of Minnesota, Harvard Divinity School, and Harvard University, where he later held an academic post from approximately 1957 to 1968.

James M. Macphail was an Indology and linguistics scholar who earned an M.A. and M.D. from the University of Glasgow. He founded the Bamdah Medical Mission in 1890 and served as a physician for the Free Church of Scotland (1889–1929).

James Mackintosh was a scholar of history, Indology, and philosophy who studied at the University of Aberdeen and University of Edinburgh. He founded and presided over the Asiatic Society of Mumbai and served as Professor at the East India Company College.

James Macnabb Campbell was an Indology, history, and archaeology scholar who studied at The Glasgow Academy and earned an M.A. from the University of Glasgow (~1862–1866). He served in the Indian Civil Service from approximately 1869 to 1897.

James Mallinson is an Indologist who studied at Eton, SOAS, and Oxford under Alexis Sanderson. He lectured at SOAS before becoming Boden Professor of Sanskrit at the University of Oxford and Director of Graduate Studies at Wolfson College, Oxford in 2023.

James Mark Shields is a scholar of religious studies, Buddhist studies, and philosophy. He held posts as Assistant and Associate Professor at Bucknell University (2007–2010, 2017) and was an Overseas Collaborative Researcher at the International Research Center for Japanese Studies (2016).
James Matthew Baskind is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Japanology who completed his Doctor of Philosophy at Yale University (attested 2006) under the supervision of Stanley Weinstein.

James McHugh, a scholar of Indology and religious studies, studied at Cambridge, Oxford, and Harvard (PhD), where his doctoral supervisors were Lawrence J. McCrea, Anne E. Monius, and Parimal G. Patil. He held posts at Cornell and the University of Southern California.
